Bishnu Sharma: 
Thank you, Yashashri. Good afternoon, everyone and a warm welcome to the Nuvoco Vistas 
earnings conference call for the quarter ended September 30th, 2026. Before we begin, just 
wanted to state what we have achieved over the past decade. 
So, this year, we have completed 10 years in the cement business. What began in 2014 with a 
single manufacturing operation at Nimbol with a 2.3 million tons of cement capacity has evolved 
into a diversified building materials company spanning cement, ready-mix concrete, and modern 
building materials. 
October 2016 marked a defining inflection point with the completion of the acquisition of 
Lafarge. This was followed by the acquisition of Emami Cement in 2020 during the COVID-19 
period, which also opened a new phase of growth. The growth agenda was further strengthened 
with the acquisition of Vadraj Cement Limited. 
Today, Nuvoco has a diversified manufacturing presence across the East, North and West and 
is well-positioned to reach 35 million tons of cement capacity by FY28, representing nearly 15-
times growth over the past decade. The journey reflects the commitment of our teams and 
continued trust of our customers, channel partners and shareholders. 
Looking ahead, the journey continues and we have multiple options for growth, including 
expansion at Gulbarga and in the North. At the same time, we continue to build up strategic 
limestone resources, which will give us the raw material security to support sustained growth 
over the long term. 
Before we open the floor for questions, I'd like to take you through the key developments of the 
quarter and how the business performed. 
Let me begin with the operating environment, which was challenging. The Middle East conflict 
which towards the end of Q1 and the beginning of Q2 appeared to be settling, escalated once 
again. This led to a sharp jump in the input prices, including petcoke, coal, granules, gypsum, 
etc. Petcoke prices, in particular, surpassed the previous peaks we witnessed between March and 
April. 
The pressure was not limited to the global front. Domestically, intense and erratic rainfall, 
especially in the East, brought thermal coal inventories at several power plants across the country 
to critical levels. As a result, coal supply was prioritized for the power sector. A consequence of

this was also reduced rake availability, which disrupted the supply chain and also led to the surge 
in domestic prices of e-auction coal. A brief trend of this is also being presented in our investor 
presentation. 
On the demand side, all-India cement demand grew during the quarter, but regional trends 
varied. The monsoon disrupted construction activity, particularly in the East, while regions with 
relatively lower rainfall saw better demand. On the other hand, prices did not improve in line 
with expectations. 
In short, it was a challenging quarter. Despite these macro challenges, the company delivered a 
resilient performance. Volume grew by 9% YoY. Revenue grew by approximately 14% and 
EBITDA grew by 11% on a YoY basis. Our strategic levers of premiumization and geo-mix 
supported this performance. Premiumization reached a historic high of 45%, whereas trade mix 
remained at 75%. 
On the project progress on Vadraj Cement Limited, the 2 million tons grinding unit at Limla 
cement plant in Surat was commissioned during the quarter. The addition not only strengthens 
Nuvoco's manufacturing and distribution presence in Western India but will enable the company 
to release much-needed capacity at Rajasthan plant for the northern market. 
At Kutch, project activities are progressing as planned, with phased operationalization planned 
from Q3 FY27. The construction of bulk cement terminal at Viramgam, Sachana, which will be 
equipped with a dedicated railway siding, is also on track. It will serve as a strategic distribution 
hub to deepen Nuvoco's presence and expand its reach across the Gujarat market. 
 
During the quarter, the company also executed agreement with CleanMax for a 46.4-megawatt 
wind-solar hybrid renewable energy project in Rajasthan. Once operational, the project is 
expected to generate approximately 100 million units of renewable electricity annually and 
deliver long-term cost certainty by reducing dependence on conventional power sources, thereby 
strengthening the company's energy mix and improving long-term cost efficiency across the 
Rajasthan operations. 
 
As we enter the upcoming quarters, we expect demand to remain healthy as monsoon conditions 
have receded in most regions. The company remains focused on delivering growth, and we'll 
continue to be watchful of the geopolitical developments. 
 
With that, I'd like to open the floor for questions. Operator, please go ahead.
